overview: Macmahon is an ASX-listed, Perth-headquartered diversified mining and civil infrastructure contractor founded in 1963, providing end-to-end surface mining, underground mining, civil construction, and equipment/mine-support services to major resource companies. The company operates almost entirely in Australia (~90% of FY26 revenue) with a growing Southeast Asia presence in Indonesia and Malaysia (~10%), servicing gold, copper, lithium, and metallurgical coal projects. Macmahon has expanded from a surface-mining specialist into a three-pillar business (Surface, Underground, Civil Infrastructure) following the August 2024 acquisition of civil contractor Decmil, targeting a more capital-light, diversified earnings mix.

business_model.summary: Macmahon is a long-life, contract mining and construction services provider that earns revenue under multi-year (often life-of-mine) contracts with major and mid-tier miners, supplemented by shorter civil infrastructure and equipment/maintenance work. Revenue is largely project- and contract-based rather than recurring in a subscription sense, but the long duration of mining contracts (5-20+ years) and a large, growing order book ($5.9bn at FY26 year-end) give strong multi-year revenue visibility.
business_model.customer_type: B2B - large-cap and mid-tier resources companies (AngloGold Ashanti, Vault Minerals, Q Coal, Talison Lithium, Greatland Gold, Genesis Minerals, Amman Mineral, BHP, Rio Tinto) plus government/infrastructure clients for civil works
business_model.geographic_mix: Australia ~90%, Southeast Asia (Indonesia/Malaysia) ~10% of FY26 revenue, with a strategic target of 15-20% from Indonesia

competitive_position.market_position: Mid-tier diversified mining and civil services contractor; smaller than global majors Thiess and Downer but an established, top-tier ASX-listed player with leading positions in Australian and Indonesian gold-sector contract mining and a growing underground and civil infrastructure franchise following the Decmil acquisition

moat_factors.description: Many contracts run 5-20+ years (e.g., Tropicana to 2033, Byerwen to 2040, Batu Hijau to 2030), creating high switching costs for clients and multi-year revenue visibility

moat_factors.factor: Deep client relationships and track record
moat_factors.description: Ninth/tenth consecutive year of meeting or exceeding market guidance; repeat contract extensions with AngloGold Ashanti, Vault Minerals, Genesis Minerals and PT Agincourt Resources

PT Amman Mineral Internasional, a major Indonesian copper/gold miner and Macmahon's largest shareholder (~45%), is also a large client (Batu Hijau contract), aligning incentives and supporting Indonesian growth
Owned Perth workshop and large surface/underground equipment fleet (Caterpillar, Hitachi, Liebherr, Epiroc, Sandvik) support in-house maintenance and rapid mobilisation
Civil infrastructure and underground segments reduce capital intensity and cyclicality relative to a pure surface-mining model

weaknesses: Low-margin, capital-intensive contract mining business (underlying EBIT(A) margin only ~7.3% in FY26) with thin pricing power versus large mining company clients
High customer concentration - top clients (AngloGold Ashanti ~18%, Vault Minerals, Q Coal) represent large shares of revenue
Commodity and client concentration in gold (~52% of FY26 revenue by commodity)
Limited scale versus global contractors Thiess and Downer, and versus larger ASX peer Perenti
Civil infrastructure business (Decmil) still maturing post-acquisition with lower margins than Surface/Underground

growth_drivers: Diversification strategy targeting roughly equal revenue split across Surface, Underground and Civil Infrastructure, with Underground and Civil each targeted to grow ~50% over 2-3 years
Indonesia expansion targeting 15-20% of group revenue (new contracts at Awak Mas, Poboya, Kucing Liar, Toka Tindung)
Large and growing tender pipeline ($25bn+ at FY26 year-end, of which $13.8bn expected to be awarded within 12 months) and order book of $5.9bn
Full integration and scale-up of Decmil civil infrastructure business, including larger (>$100m) project wins and potential partnerships with international tier-one civil players
Nifty Copper Complex whole-of-mine alliance with Cyprium Metals - a new service model with 20-year mine life potential
ROACE improvement program - target raised from 20% to >25%, driving free cash flow generation and capital efficiency
Continued deleveraging enabling increased shareholder returns (dividend payout ratio raised to 35-45% of underlying EPS for FY27) and capacity for M&A
Inclusion in the S&P/ASX 300 Index (March 2026), improving index-fund visibility and liquidity
Monetisation of the non-core Homeground Gladstone accommodation village asset acquired with Decmil

business.description: A relatively small number of large clients (AngloGold Ashanti, Vault Minerals, Q Coal, Talison Lithium) represent a significant share of revenue; loss or non-renewal of a major contract would be material
Project delays, cost overruns, and early contract terminations in a complex multi-site operating environment can materially impact financial performance and reputation
Failure to win or extend contracts at appropriate economic returns could erode the order book and future earnings
Ongoing shortage of skilled labour in Australian mining/construction and surging demand for diversified services could constrain growth and increase costs
A workplace fatality occurred at Fosterville Gold Mine in December 2025, underscoring inherent safety risk in underground/surface mining operations that can also cause reputational and contract risk

financial.description: Net debt/EBITDA reduced to 0.28x and gearing to 13.0% at FY26 year-end (from 19.0%/0.42x a year earlier) following the debt-funded Decmil acquisition, now well within internal guiderails (<1.0x, <30% gearing)
Surface mining remains capital-intensive (FY26 capex $204.3m); sustaining and growth capex requirements can pressure free cash flow in growth years
Growing Indonesian and Malaysian operations expose the group to foreign currency fluctuations, partially managed through natural hedging
Exposure to contingent liabilities disclosed in financial statement notes that could convert into actual liabilities

regulatory.description: AASB S2 Climate-related Disclosures took effect from FY26; Macmahon must build governance, data and reporting systems across Australia, Indonesia and Malaysia, with risk of misreporting or non-compliance
Operations in Indonesia and Malaysia carry higher sovereign risk than Australia, including exposure to bribery/corruption, civil unrest, and evolving local regulation
Shifts in Australian industrial relations legislation or increased union activism could disrupt operations covered by Enterprise Agreements

macro.description: Revenue is skewed to gold (~52%) with additional exposure to copper, lithium and metallurgical coal; contractor activity and new contract awards are sensitive to client commodity price cycles, though existing life-of-mine contracts partly insulate near-term revenue
Management repeatedly cites global trade tensions and macro uncertainty as contributing to commodity price volatility and elevated input costs (e.g., fuel)
Effective borrowing cost of ~6% on debt facilities; rate moves affect finance costs, though net debt is now low relative to EBITDA
FY26 characterised by 'significantly elevated fuel costs' per management commentary

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Australian and Southeast Asian mining services sector benefiting from resilient gold and copper prices, robust lithium and coal production volumes, and continued resources capex cycle; broader ASX mining-services peer group (NRW, Perenti) also reporting strong order books in 2026
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately cyclical - tied to miners' capex and production decisions and underlying commodity prices, but partially smoothed by long-dated life-of-mine contracts and diversification into civil infrastructure and underground mining, which management explicitly cites as reducing cyclicality
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate - net debt is now modest (0.28x EBITDA, 13.0% gearing at FY26 year-end) so direct interest expense sensitivity is limited, but higher rates raise financing costs on equipment/bank facilities and could dampen clients' capex appetite

recent_developments.event: Reported record FY2026 (year ended 30 June 2026) results: revenue $2.6bn (+8%), underlying EBITDA $393.8m (+2%), underlying EBIT(A) $190.1m (+11%), underlying NPAT $114.8m (+12%), statutory NPAT $101.1m; tenth consecutive year of meeting or exceeding market guidance; net debt cut to $111.1m (gearing 13.0%, ND/EBITDA 0.28x); final dividend 1.25 cps fully franked, taking FY26 total to 2.20 cps (+47% YoY)
Issued FY2027 guidance of revenue $2.85bn-$3.05bn and underlying EBIT(A) $205m-$225m; raised dividend payout ratio target to 35-45% of underlying EPS (from 30-45%)
Macmahon included in the S&P/ASX 300 Index
Amman Mineral CEO Arief Sidarto appointed to the Board as a Non-Independent Non-Executive Director, maintaining Amman's board representation
Decmil received a notice of award from Rio Tinto for the West Angelas Sustaining Project (WASP), valued at $120m, plus a further $30m non-process infrastructure/medical centre contract
A Macmahon employee fatality occurred at the Fosterville Gold Mine, highlighted by the Chair as a serious safety event
Byerwen Coal Mine contract extended for three years, valued at $792m, with an option to extend a further two years to $1.32bn total value
Board renewal: Greg Evans became Chair following Hamish Tyrwhitt's retirement; Suzan Pervan, Tom Quinn and Arief Sidarto joined as new Non-Executive Directors; Maree Arnason and David Gibbs departed
Analysts (Simply Wall St) lifted fair value estimate for MAH from A$0.79 to A$0.90; consensus analyst rating remains Buy with price targets clustering around A$0.75-A$1.02
Letters of intent received for restart contracts at Mount Carlton Gold Mine (~$150m, with Wolfram Ltd/Bumi Resources) and Wonawinta Silver Project (~$190m, with Manuka Resources)

items.notes: Up from FY26 guidance of $2.6bn-$2.8bn (which was itself achieved: FY26 actual revenue $2.62bn); $2.2bn already secured for FY27 against an order book of $5.9bn and tender pipeline of $25bn
Up from FY26 guidance of $180m-$195m (FY26 actual $190.1m, upper half of range)
Increased from 30-45% policy used for FY26; FY26 total dividend 2.20 cps, up 47% YoY, at a 41% payout ratio
Raised from a prior >20% target after ROACE reached 22.0% in FY26 (21.2% at 1H26)
Part of the roughly equal three-way Surface/Underground/Civil revenue mix strategy
FY26 actual Indonesia mix was ~10% of Group revenue

guidance.management_commentary: Chair Greg Evans and CEO Michael Finnegan struck a confident tone on FY27, citing gold's continued strong performance, a diversified revenue base across mining and civil infrastructure and across commodities, and a robust $25bn tender pipeline ($13.8bn expected to convert within 12 months) as underpinning the outlook, despite acknowledging ongoing commodity price volatility, elevated fuel costs and global capital market uncertainty.

bull_case: Ten consecutive years of meeting or beating market guidance demonstrates unusually disciplined execution and forecasting credibility for a contractor in a cyclical sector

Successful Decmil integration has diversified the earnings base into lower-capital-intensity civil infrastructure and underground mining, reducing reliance on capital-heavy surface mining and smoothing cyclicality
Strong and growing order book ($5.9bn) and tender pipeline ($25bn, with $13.8bn expected to convert within 12 months) provide multi-year revenue visibility well beyond FY27 guidance

Balance sheet has been rapidly deleveraged (gearing down to 13.0%, net debt/EBITDA to 0.28x) while still funding growth capex and lifting the dividend payout ratio, giving optionality for further M&A or accelerated shareholder returns

Exposure to structurally supported commodities (gold ~52% of revenue, plus copper and lithium) benefiting from strong current prices and investor sentiment, alongside diversification into renewables-related civil works
bear_case: Inherently low-margin, capital-intensive contract mining model (underlying EBIT(A) margin only ~7.3% in FY26) leaves limited room for error on cost overruns or contract mispricing
High revenue concentration in gold and in a handful of large clients (AngloGold Ashanti, Vault Minerals, Q Coal) creates vulnerability to a single lost contract or a gold price downturn

Majority shareholder PT Amman Mineral Internasional (~45% stake, also a major client and board nominee) creates potential governance and minority-shareholder alignment questions, and limits free float/liquidity

Civil infrastructure (Decmil) segment still carries lower margins than the core mining business and is less than two years into full integration, so execution risk on larger (>$100m) project wins remains unproven at scale

A December 2025 employee fatality at Fosterville highlights ongoing safety and reputational tail risk inherent to underground/surface mining operations, which can also jeopardise client relationships and contract renewals
Small-cap, thinly analyst-covered stock (only ~2 analysts) with a wide range of fair value estimates (A$0.75-A$1.02), implying limited institutional scrutiny and potential for valuation dislocation
